payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #753, decision 0089's slice 1 store half (slice 1a): every run keeps one summary row, written by triggers and by the writer's fold in each append's transaction, backfilled and caught up at a writer's open, compared by `brokkr doctor`. No reader changes in this slice.

Operator rulings:
- 2026-10-19, on PR #769, verbatim: "accept all for 0089". Decision 0089 is ACCEPTED, every one of its 15 "Asked of the operator" choices taken as recommended (recorded on #753): three projections (this slice builds `run_summary` only); the append carries its caller's fold; triggers keep presence, head and acknowledgement for every writer and DATABASE_SCHEMA stays 1; integrity at fleet level by the head check alone, with the full chain check at a run's opening, at every verb that acts on a run, and in `brokkr doctor`; every column bounded per ruling 2's table; the generated `lane` key and `order_at`; rows behind their head caught up; migration by a writer's backfill and a read-only reader falling back to #744's kept read; checkpoint bodies inline; slice 1 is the fleet. Ruling 11: slice 1 "may land as two pull requests, the store's half first". This is that first half.
- Operator's words framing #753 (2026-10-18): "yes, draft the summary-table decision, and add pagination to it. Then it can grow as much as it wants, we are still in the milliseconds. Also, 81mb memory for one page TUI is nonesense, don't you think?"; "the backend data that with synthesize and design should be usable for the other views as well, so we make all the views blazing fast".
- Decision 0014 (readouts read-only); decision 0001 (the journal is the hash-chained truth); 2026-09-26, the threat model.

READ decision 0089 (docs/decisions/0089-every-readout-reads-a-page-of-what-the-writer-keeps.md) rulings 1-8 and 11 first: they are the acceptance.

The branch story-753-s1a ends at 59c56421, cut from main 231692c6; it merges clean with main dd46ade4. Five commits, 53 files (+3773/-307):
- 32abfcbf (story run implement-story-753-fleet-one-su-a84c7b37): run_summary with ruling 2's columns, the generated `lane` (ruling 6's CASE) and `order_at`, the index; the triggers on runs, events and quarantine_acknowledgements (ruling 3); the writer's fold carried through every append (Store::carry; the engine's appends in engine/fence.rs, the checkpoint sink's append_chain, engine.rs's two run/started append_next calls; operator verbs; import); ruling 2's bounds; create_run gains import's RUN_ID_MAX (StoreError::RunIdTooLong); brokkr-core's pure projection (summary::Account and friends), `open_severity` with its closing marks (residual::closings, Mark, Citation) and `stamp::parse_millis` moved from brokkr-view; the backfill (one run per transaction, a meta key) and the catch-up of the behind lane at every writable open; every_run_reads_as_its_fold over the engine scenarios and every fixture journal; a_cut_first_line_titles_as_its_feature; the layering binding (crates/brokkr-cli/tests/layering/projection.rs). Measured, release, warm: backfill 4.75 s (4.50 s at load 9), VmHWM 10.1 MB; a steady reopen under 1 ms; an append's median 796 -> 958 us and 787 -> 956 us (+162 to +169 us).
- 2ec7dfc7, 9ac9fec9: the doctor's comparison (summary_disagreements, one run id at a time, one snapshot) and every writer's run held at its head in tests.
- Its second review ruled REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD (high): the doctor's sweep skipped a corrupt run whose row was behind (compared() returned Behind before loading), so a broken chain passed `brokkr doctor` forever; and (medium) the catch-up collected every behind run id into a Vec.
- 046687af (fix round 753s1b; review residual LOW, no security residual): the sweep reads every run whole, behind or at head, and reports one that does not load as Disagreement::Unread with the store's error; the catch-up walks the behind lane by keyset one id at a time (a dhat heap test at two sizes, crates/brokkr-store/tests/summary_heap.rs); append_chain records the test binding; refold_once's head guard bound; a test renamed.
- 59c56421 (fix round 753s1c; review CLEAN): the four coverage gaps closed by failure tests with exact variant and text (mark_backfilled's insert, Listed::of's unknown run, the refold's write, and catch_up returning a non-contention refusal rather than swallowing it).
- Host exact coverage on 59c56421 is 100% (64753/64753 lines, 8348/8348 branches, 8329/8329 functions), and host lints hold.
- Public API (quality/public-api): brokkr-core +69 lines (the `summary` module: Account, Bounded, Hired, Listing, Refused, Ruled and the rest; the `stamp` module with parse_millis; residual::Citation, Mark, closings and open_severity; fold::Cursor::hire); brokkr-store +16 (Disagreement {Column, Missing, Unread} with Display; StoreError::RunIdTooLong; Store::carry; Store::summary_disagreements); brokkr-view -1 (js::parse_millis moved to brokkr-core).
- Carried findings: LOW (exotic): an acknowledgement operator carrying NUL is cut by SQLite's substr at the NUL while `kept` takes chars() of the whole string, so the doctor names a healthy API write an ack_operator disagreement; CLI argv cannot carry NUL. LOW (test infrastructure): `settle` records `wrote(run_id)` even after an append_chain that landed no row, so the drop check can panic loud on an untouched run (cfg(test) only). INFO: an events row hand-planted under a raw connection with foreign keys off, for a run with no `runs` row, is walked by no sweep (a deliberate hand edit).

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, on the HEAD binary and tests (the base is the merge-base 231692c6):
1. Decision 0089 rulings 1-4 and 8, as accepted, are what the code does: ruling 2's columns and bounds (cut at a character boundary; the whole values last; `title` from feature_line agreeing as ruling 2 states); ruling 3's triggers and the writer's fold in the same transaction; ruling 6's `lane` CASE token for token and `order_at`; ruling 8's migration (one short immediate transaction, then a per-run backfill outside the lock, a meta key, a resumable cut) with DATABASE_SCHEMA still 1 and a read-only open migrating and writing nothing (decision 0014). Name any divergence.
2. Integrity (ruling 5 and Asked 4): reproduce on the HEAD binary a broken chain planted as an older writer's events (behind) and as corruption below an unmoved head (at head), and see `brokkr doctor` report each with the exact text. Then try a path not yet tried (a truncated envelope, a row removed below the head, an acknowledgement at a stale head) and see the sweep report it. Confirm no reader yet trusts a row: the console and `brokkr runs` still read #744's kept read, and the engine decides on its own fold (the layering binding).
3. The fold is one derivation (decision 0071 ruling 7): every_run_reads_as_its_fold holds over every fixture journal imported fresh and after the engine scenarios; parse_millis and open_severity have one home (brokkr-core) and brokkr-view's output is byte-unchanged (its existing tests unchanged).
4. Cost: re-measure the append's added median and the backfill's time and peak on the generated journal (the branch's generator), and say whether either surprises against ruling 9's intent (ruling 9's page budgets are slice 1b's).
5. Standards and scope: CC 15 or under and 100 lines or under for every new or changed function (cargo crap); quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api (the three listing diffs above, exactly); "mutants in the diff: brokkr-core" (quality/mutants/brokkr-core.missed.txt stays empty: run `cargo mutants -p brokkr-core --in-diff` on the diff if available); nothing under contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/; no engine/broker* hunk; engine.rs only the append/carry hunks.
6. For the PR: name every ruling needed. Expected: (a) the public API additions in brokkr-core and brokkr-store and the brokkr-view removal; (b) StoreError::RunIdTooLong's refusal text at create_run (import's check, now at the writer); (c) the NUL LOW (accept under the threat model, or refuse NUL in an acknowledgement at the edge); (d) the append's added ~165 us median, for the operator's information; (e) the test-infrastructure LOW as a follow-up. Recommend for each, and name slice 1b (the readers, paging, ruling 5's head check on a page, ruling 9's budgets, redraw only on change) as the follow-up.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-core --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-store --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-view --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib --locked (timeout 590) and --test it; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- doctor:: fleet:: import:: export:: suppressions:: machine_proof:: doc_samples:: doc_truth:: layering:: (timeout 590 each); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; `cargo crap --path <crate>/src --format json` for every function you add or change; git diff --check.

Other work runs in parallel. Decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat; PR #778) is in brokkr-runtime engine/broker* and brokkr-protocol hands*. #614 (landing) edits brokkr-cli tests/doc_truth.rs and packaging.rs. #288 slice N (PR #780) edits brokkr-runtime agents/load/tests.rs. This landing touches none of their files.

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" if a fix is needed, and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

RULING 1 (the engine decides on its own fold, never a row) HOLDS. crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/operator.rs gains decided(store, run_id, events), which folds via brokkr_core::summary::Account::whole and hands the account to Store::carry; read_back uses it. engine/replay.rs holds Replay.account: Option<Account> and caught_up(&mut store) re-carries it every turn, with a doc comment citing ruling 1. No decision path reads run_summary; the layering test crates/brokkr-cli/tests/layering/projection.rs asserts the only production readers of run_summary/summary_disagreements are the doctor, and that no brokkr-runtime production source names them (it passes, including its planted-scan removal control).

RULING 2 (columns and bounds) HOLDS. crates/brokkr-store/src/summary.rs holds the table exactly as the ruling-2 table states it: stamps cut at a character boundary to at most 40 bytes (the run_summary_stamp_bounded trigger steps back past at most three continuation bytes; I verified the CASE arithmetic and that Bounded::within in brokkr-core gives the same prefix for the same input, so writer and doctor agree), phase/rule/seat names 64 bytes, park_reason 256, refusal words 512, feature_line 1024 (first non-empty trimmed line, cut at a char boundary), ack operator/reason/at 64/256/40 by substr, folded columns from the fold, head columns and last_at_ms by the writer, lane and generated order_at = COALESCE(last_at_ms, i64::MAX), and the whole values (feature, residuals, *_whole) last in the row. residual_count counts open findings (findings without a closing mark), matching the fleet's residual cell; residual_open is the moved open_severity. created_at is bounded at 40 while runs.created_at keeps the whole (created_at_whole).

RULING 3 (the writer keeps the model in every insert's transaction; triggers keep presence/head/ack for every writer) HOLDS. judge() (summary.rs:409) is called inside append_once/append chain_once/create_run_once/adopt_once transactions and writes only when the carried account is the sealed run's and stands at the head the append chained onto (carried.account.head() != found -> Settled::Lost, nothing folded, account dropped). create_run carries Account::empty so a new run's row is written in its own creation transaction. The three triggers keep presence (AFTER INSERT ON runs), head and last_recorded_at for events at or beyond the row's head (NEW.seq > head_seq), and acknowledgements standing at the row's head (head_seq = NEW.head_seq AND head_hash = NEW.head_hash, the same test as standing()). Older writers leave the row behind; verified on the HEAD release binary with a hand-planted older-writer run: row present, head_seq 11, folded_seq NULL, lane behind.

RULING 4 (the summary equals a fresh fold, and a test says so) HOLDS. every_run_reads_as_its_fold (test_support.rs) reads every run whole and compares the row's written+kept columns to Summary::of(Account::whole) first-difference; it passes over all fixture journals (refused ones re-planted as older writers) and after the runtime scenarios (a_bridge_command_writes_the_summary_of_the_fold_it_decided_on, an_operator_verb_writes_the_summary_of_the_fold_it_decided_on, a_driven_run_leaves_its_summary_at_its_head - all green in this review). The doctor's report_summaries reports each Disagreement as a failure. The drop check (a_writer_store_checks_every_run_when_it_is_dropped, plus the lost-account and failing-test variants) binds test stores to their folds.

RULING 5/7 (integrity: the sweep reads every run whole; a row is placed by its fold) HOLDS, including the second review's HIGH fix: compared() (summary.rs:662-695) loads the run's whole journal and returns Disagreement::Unread when it does not load, BEFORE the behind test, so a corrupt behind run is named rather than passed. each_run_compared walks run ids by key one at a time and holds nothing of a run past its comparison; summary_heap.rs binds the memory (largest run's) and the doctor comparison one run at a time. FINDING (carried, LOW, exotic): an acknowledgement whose operator or reason carries a NUL byte. The trigger copies it with SQLite substr, which stops at the NUL (verified: substr/length truncate at it), while kept() counts chars of the whole string, so the doctor would name a healthy API write an ack_operator disagreement forever. Reachable only through a bridge/API write - CLI argv cannot carry NUL. Not realistic accidental misuse under the 2026-09-26 threat model, and the failure is fail-noisy (a false positive), never fail-open. Recommendation: refuse NUL in an acknowledgement's operator/reason at the edge (one check in acknowledge_quarantine) as the cleaner endgame; accepting it under the threat model is also defensible. Not required for this slice.

FINDING (carried, LOW, test-infra): Store::settle records binding.wrote(run_id) even when an append landed no row (e.g. append_chain under contention returns before any insert), so a test that expects a write may panic at drop on a test bug rather than a summary bug. cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support")) only - cannot mislead production.
